tweets: Lingaraja Temple, Bhubaneswar — Kalinga architecture, 11th century. Its rekha deul climbs nearly 55 metres in receding tiers of dressed sandstone, block fitted to block and held by weight alone: not a trace of mortar in the whole tower.

Here Śiva is worshipped as Harihara, fused with Viṣṇu — one form, two gods. The temple anchors Bhubaneswar, long called the "Temple City" for the hundreds of shrines still standing around it. Follow @yddoseOfHistory for your daily dose of history
